Intelligent Research Assistant
Project Report
4.2
Vector Storage with FAISS
FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is heavily utilized to optimize the retrieval mech-
anism. Rather than hosting an external vector database (which increases latency and
deployment complexity), the application maintains independent FAISS indices directly
on the local filesystem.
Each Workspace possesses its own physical directory and its own faiss.index file.
This design choice provides absolute data isolation.
When a user queries Workspace
A, the system physically cannot leak vectors from Workspace B, solving major security
concerns in multi-tenant environments.
When a query is made, FAISS executes an exhaustive inner-product search. Because
local FAISS runs entirely in RAM via highly optimized C++ binaries, retrieving the
top-5 relevant chunks from a database of 100,000 chunks takes less than 5 milliseconds
on standard CPU hardware.
